mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a supply-driven inflation scare that will pressure the Fed to tighten policy and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE does not rise
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 55% of triggered instances, indicating the inflation scare was transient or already priced in.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid 0.5% rise in the unemployment rate over 3 months, if accompanied by a simultaneous decline in payroll employment, signals a labor market recession that will weigh on consumer spending and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months and PAYEMS declines
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) both show positive YoY growth during the signal period, indicating the labor market weakness is not broad-based.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% hike in the federal funds rate, if not already at a restrictive level (> 4%), signals a tightening monetary policy that will raise borrowing costs and pressure S&P 500 earnings, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 1 month and level < 4%
failure_condition: SPX volatility (VIX) declines and credit spreads (BofA ML US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread) tighten during the signal period, indicating the rate hike was well-telegraphed and already priced in.

mechanism_narrative: A 5% YoY decline in housing starts, if accompanied by a simultaneous decline in retail sales, signals a broad-based demand slowdown that will weigh on S&P 500 earnings and produce negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% YoY and RSAFS declines YoY
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index) rises and auto sales (Light Weight Vehicle Sales: Autos) show positive MoM growth during the signal period, indicating the demand slowdown is not broad-based.

mechanism_narrative: A 2% YoY rise in the core CPI index, if accompanied by a simultaneous rise in industrial production, signals a supply-driven inflation surge that will pressure the Fed to tighten policy and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 2% YoY and INDPRO rises > 1% YoY
failure_condition: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate (T10YIE) declines and the dollar (DXY) strengthens during the signal period, indicating the inflation surge is transitory and already priced in.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% decline in the unemployment rate over 3 months, if accompanied by a simultaneous rise in payroll employment, signals a labor market boom that will boost consumer spending and produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines > 0.5pp in 3 months and PAYEMS rises
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (AHETPI) show negative YoY growth and the labor force participation rate (CIVPART) declines during the signal period, indicating the labor market strength is not sustainable.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% cut in the federal funds rate, if already at an accommodative level (< 2%), signals a dovish monetary policy pivot that will boost risk appetite and produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines > 0.5pp in 1 month and level < 2%
failure_condition: The 2-year Treasury yield (DGS2) rises and the dollar (DXY) strengthens during the signal period, indicating the rate cut was a 'hawkish dove' move and not a genuine easing pivot.
